title: Triangle with slanted sides
observableEvidence: Finds the area of a non-right triangle from its base and perpendicular height, ignoring the slanted side lengths, and labels the result in square units.
prompt: The figure shows a triangle whose bottom side is 21 centimeters long. Its two slanted sides are 10 centimeters and 17 centimeters long. The dashed line from the top corner meets the bottom side at a right angle and is 8 centimeters long. What is the area of the triangle? Include the unit in your answer.
solutionRepresentation: The height must meet the base at a right angle, so use the dashed 8 cm line, not a slanted side. Area = 1/2 × 21 × 8 = 1/2 × 168 = 84 square centimeters. The 10 cm and 17 cm sides are not used.
solutionMethod: Pair the base with the perpendicular height (not a slanted side), multiply, take half, and label the result in square centimeters.

deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Whole-answer match after case, spacing and trailing-punctuation normalization; no substring parts. The square-centimeter unit is required: a bare number, or the number with a linear or cubic unit, is not accepted.

hintSteps.prompt: The area of a triangle uses a base and the height that meets that base at a right angle. A slanted side is not a height.
hintSteps.question: Which length in the figure meets the 21-centimeter side at a right angle?

hintSteps.prompt: Two copies of this triangle fit together into a parallelogram with the same base and height, so the triangle is half of base times height.
hintSteps.question: What is the base times the height, before you take half?

hintSteps.prompt: A different triangle has a base of 8 meters, two slanted sides of 5 meters each and a perpendicular height of 3 meters. Its area is 1/2 × 8 × 3 = 12 square meters; the 5-meter sides are not used.
hintSteps.question: Using the same rule, which two lengths from this figure do you multiply, and what is half of their product?
